name: Zanda vs Jane App
title: Zanda vs Jane App: Allied Health Practice Management Comparison
description: Compare Zanda (formerly Power Diary) and Jane App for allied health practices. See differences in pricing, features, telehealth, and international support.

summary.bottom_line: Both Zanda and Jane App serve allied health practices globally. Zanda is the more affordable option with lower starting prices and is popular in Australia/UK. Jane App offers stronger North American billing, AI Scribe, and exceptional customer support. Choose Zanda for maximum affordability and international use; choose Jane App for North American practices needing AI documentation and better billing integrations.

sections.heading: Zanda vs Jane App: Overview
sections.content: Zanda (formerly Power Diary, rebranded November 2024) and Jane App are both cloud-based practice management platforms designed for allied health practices including physiotherapy, chiropractic, psychology, massage therapy, and more. Zanda is Australian-based and popular in Australia, UK, and Europe. Jane App is Canadian-based with strong North American presence. Both offer scheduling, clinical notes, online booking, and telehealth. Zanda is known for affordable pricing while Jane App is known for exceptional customer support (2026 Silver Stevie Award winner) and AI documentation features.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Zanda is significantly more affordable: Starter at $19/month (up to 1,000 appointments) vs. Jane App Balance at $54/month (only 20 appointments). For unlimited appointments, Zanda Growth is $49/month vs. Jane App Practice at $79/month. Additional practitioners cost $9.50/month with Zanda vs. $5/full-timer with Jane. However, Jane App includes more features like AI Scribe ($15/mo add-on) and stronger billing integrations. For pure affordability, Zanda wins; for feature completeness, Jane App may justify the higher price.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: Jane App's key advantages are AI Scribe for documentation, strong Canadian billing (Telus Health), US insurance billing add-on, and award-winning customer support. Zanda's advantages are lower pricing, ISO 27001 certification, and strong presence in Australia/UK markets. Both have mobile apps, telehealth, online booking, and multi-location support. Zanda added AI-driven features as part of its 2024 rebrand, but Jane's AI Scribe is more established. For practices prioritizing AI documentation, Jane App has the edge.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Choose based on your location, budget, and feature needs:

recommendations.when: You're in Australia, UK, or Europe, want the lowest possible pricing, don't need advanced North American billing, or prefer ISO 27001 certification
You're in North America (especially Canada), want AI Scribe documentation, need Telus Health or US insurance billing, or value award-winning customer support
You're a multi-disciplinary allied health practice with primarily self-pay clients and flexible on pricing—both are solid choices

faqs.q: Is Zanda the same as Power Diary?
faqs.a: Yes, Zanda is the rebranded name for Power Diary as of November 2024. It's the same practice management software with added AI-driven features. Existing Power Diary users transitioned to the Zanda brand.

faqs.q: Which is cheaper: Zanda or Jane App?
faqs.a: Zanda is significantly cheaper: $19/month starter vs. Jane's $54/month. For unlimited appointments, Zanda is $49/month vs. Jane's $79/month. Zanda is the clear winner for budget-conscious practices.

faqs.q: Does Jane App work for Australian practices?
faqs.a: Jane App can work for Australian practices but is Canadian-based with stronger North American integrations. Zanda (formerly Power Diary) is Australian-based and may offer better regional support and integrations for Australian practices.

faqs.q: Which has better AI documentation features?
faqs.a: Jane App's AI Scribe ($15/mo) is more established and specifically designed for clinical documentation. Zanda added AI features in its 2024 rebrand, but Jane's offering is more mature and widely used.
